body: LOCAL-OPENABILITY ACCEPTANCE COURT, separating owner law from proposal. Owner-derived portion: place the unpacked bundle in a directory whose path contains a space and non-ASCII characters; navigate an ordinary browser directly to file:///.../preview.html; start no HTTP listener and perform no build, install, terminal, or preprocessing step. The entry point must produce a usable initial document under that file origin, including a visible semantic/result status rather than a blank shell. Relative CSS, scripts, and assets may participate if they work from file://. Proposed additional assertion: the first view exposes the manifest identity and either canonical text plus model status or an explicit refused/unestablished state, so easy opening cannot hide a failed semantic outcome. Explicit non-assertions: this court does not forbid JavaScript, remote requests, multiple bundle-local files, or loss of enhanced behavior when scripting is disabled. Record requested network URLs as diagnostics for the separate offline/assets policy; do not silently promote them into owner law. It should also kill the common implementation that fetches sibling JSON at runtime and therefore works under localhost but fails under a file origin.
